NextAuth's own sign-in/callback/session/csrf endpoints (export const { GET, POST } = handlers — not detected by the export-function regex, so this file's methods here are hand-verified from src/lib/auth.js, not regex-extracted). Inherently must be reachable pre-session; creates/updates sessions and, on OAuth callback, User rows via the Prisma adapter. This is a 5th public+stateChanging route NOT in the Task 2 brief's enumerated exception list (stripe/webhook, webhooks/*, auth/register, contact) — flagged prominently in the task report for explicit sign-off. NextAuth has its own CSRF-token protection for the credentials flow, independent of this app's Task 3 origin-check work. Origin check N/A here specifically: must be reachable pre-session (sign-in itself), and NextAuth carries its own independent CSRF-token protection for the credentials flow — layering this app's verifyOrigin on top is out of scope for Task 3.

Task 3 origin-check target. Unlike the 13 synchronous /api/generate/* tool routes (which go through handleGeneration in src/lib/generation-handler.js and accept EITHER a session OR an API key via authenticateApiKey), this route calls getCurrentUserWithCredits() only — API-key callers cannot use the async submission path. Classified 'user', not 'mixed(user+apikey)'; flagged as an inconsistency worth a product decision (intentional scope-limit vs. a gap). Task 3: verifyOrigin wired unconditionally on POST — this route authenticates via session cookie only (getCurrentUserWithCredits, no authenticateApiKey branch), so unlike the mixed(user+apikey) generate/* tool routes there is no api-key path to exempt. Phase 4A Task 5: no auth/originCheck/stateChanging change — this route now enqueues a durable GenerationJob (src/lib/job-queue.js) instead of calling the provider inline; it ends with the credit reservation ACTIVE (settle moved to the job runner / completion webhook) rather than settled synchronously as before.

Task 3 origin-check target for the session-cookie half of `mixed`; the API-key half is a bearer credential immune to CSRF. Auth/billing/rate-limit logic lives entirely in src/lib/generation-handler.js's handleGeneration (authenticateApiKey → getCurrentUserWithCredits fallback; checkRateLimit(user.id, `/api/generate/${tool}`)). Task 3 decision: NOT wired to verifyOrigin. Correctly scoping this needs auth-path branching (apply the check only on the session-cookie branch, mirroring how generate/async is auth-only-by-session and was wired unconditionally) — deferred to a follow-up task across all 13 mixed(user+apikey) generate/* tool routes, not done in Task 3.

ANOMALY: GET with a side effect — unconditionally calls recordTemplateUse() on every successful call, decrementing usage against the caller's TemplatePurchase. Violates HTTP GET safety/idempotency and is reachable via a plain cookie-riding cross-site GET (e.g. an / tag) with no CSRF protection possible for a GET (Task 3's origin-check work targets state-changing requests broadly, but GET requests are typically exempted by convention — this route is exactly why that convention is dangerous here). Recommend converting to POST in a follow-up. Task 3 (final round): verifyOrigin wired on the GET handler itself — deliberate exception to "GET stays open", because this GET has a real side effect (recordTemplateUse) and is the anomaly this note already flags. Origin/Referer fallback still catches a cross-site /-tag GET, which is exactly the vector described above.
